# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review. Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests. ## Wiki index - [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md) - [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md) - [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md) - [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md) - [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md) - [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md) ## Main project file The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml). Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md) aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job. Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue. Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run. ## Shell timing When writing shell scripts, always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands. Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command; the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in interactive shell commands. ## Ideas Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under `./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as `ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`. ## Links in handoffs When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use the `codex://threads/` URL format. When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days. ## OpenCode GitHub Actions To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user. Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation. The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session, verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward. When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status. Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`, which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit. Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account. Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only. Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota. Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound. Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries. Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save. Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker. To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with `gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`, then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ` to discover the host and port and SSH with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper. When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when live log evidence can be collected. For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh ``` The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from `_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while inspecting the runner. ## Mac SSH access The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as: ```sh ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running. ## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`: ```sh bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub ``` For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and use the same key: ```sh ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \ -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \ -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \ -p runner@.agentsweb.space ``` Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never print secrets while inspecting a worker. ---PROMPT--- I want you to build a first-person shooter at the level of the most recent Call of Duty games. It should be utterly perfect, visually beautiful, with every single thing done at AAA quality—from textures to physics to anything you could think of. Fan out sub-agents and have sub-agents tackle each one individually so that the game is utterly perfect. Have a separate sub-agent check each item visually to ensure it looks triple A. That separate sub-agent should be a really harsh critic, and if it doesn't look triple A, keep iterating until it does. Don't stop until each sub-agent is utterly wowed with the quality when compared with the actual Call of Duty game. It should literally compare them side by side blind and say which one looks better. Do this in ThreeJS. Continue iterating until it's utterly perfect. Fan out sub-agents and ultracode. ---README HEAD---

A Full Game or App Out. 🚀 [![Status](https://img.shields.io/badge/status-🔥%20works-brightgreen?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/denaidark/OhMyGithub?style=for-the-badge&logo=github)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/issues) [![GitHub Actions](https://img.shields.io/badge/GitHub%20Actions-automated-2088FF?style=for-the-badge&logo=githubactions&logoColor=white)](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub/actions) [![OpenCode](https://img.shields.io/badge/powered%20by-OpenCode-111111?style=for-the-badge)](https://opencode.ai/) ```text ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗ ║ DESCRIBE IT → BUILD IT → TEST IT → PLAY IT ║ ║ ║ ║ One GitHub issue. One prompt. A complete project. ║ ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝ ``` **No API keys to configure. No server to maintain. No local setup maze.**
--- ## 🤯 What Is OMG? > **Your GitHub issue becomes the product brief.** OMG (Oh My GitHub) is an automated GitHub Actions workflow for creating complete browser games and app projects from one natural-language prompt. Write what you want in an issue and add the `OpenCode` label. OpenCode checks out the project, uses the shared skills, builds the experience, runs tests, verifies the result, and publishes an immutable OmGithub project link from the finished commit. Yes, it creates the code. Yes, it runs the verification loop. Yes, it can expose the result in a temporary browser URL. ## 🧠 TL;DR 1. Open a GitHub issue. 2. Describe the game or app you want. 3. Add the `OpenCode` label to the issue. 4. Let GitHub Actions build, test, verify, and propose the result. ```text Your idea → GitHub issue → OpenCode → tests → immutable OmGithub project ``` ## ⚡ Quick Start Create an issue in your repository with a concrete request: ```text Build a neon asteroid game. Requirements: - Arrow-key movement - Score and restart button - Win and lose states - Responsive browser layout - Run tests and verify it in a browser ``` That is the whole user-facing workflow. GitHub Actions handles the runner, OpenCode handles implementation, and the workflow handles verification plus the immutable project commit. To run against an existing non-default branch, end the issue title with a `branch: ` directive. The directive selects the checkout and is removed before the issue body is sent to OpenCode: ```sh gh issue create \ --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub \ --title "Custom branch smoke test branch: codex/omgithub-site" \ --body "Build a tiny browser page." \ --label Goal \ --label OpenCode ``` The GitHub App validates the branch before dispatching. If the directive is absent, the repository default branch remains the target. ## 🌍 What Can You Build? | 🎯 Use case | ✨ Example | |---|---| | 🎮 Arcade games | Breakout, Space Invaders, Asteroids, Match-3 | | 🧩 Puzzle games | Word games, logic puzzles, card games | | 🏃 Interactive demos | Physics experiments, simulations, visual toys | | 📊 Dashboards | Filters, charts, status panels, analytics views | | 🛠️ Internal tools | Trackers, generators, small workflow apps | | 🌐 Landing pages | Product pages, portfolios, interactive showcases | | 🧪 Prototypes | Turn a product idea into a runnable proof of concept | | 📱 Browser apps | Responsive tools that work on desktop and mobile | ## 🧰 What Happens Automatically? > **The workflow is the product.** - 📥 Checks out your repository and the shared OpenCode skills. - 🏷️ Synchronizes `model/*` and `skill/*` labels. - 🧭 Reads issue labels to select the model and requested skills. - 🤖 Runs OpenCode against the current project. - 🧪 Runs a second verification prompt after implementation. - 🌐 Starts the app and checks the local runtime. - 🔗 Creates a temporary public preview URL when verification passes. - 🔀 Creates and pushes an `opencode/` branch. - 🕹️ Adds an `Open Project` link backed by the repository path, with full-commit links retained for compatibility. - 💬 Posts progress and access details back to the issue. - 🧹 Cleans up temporary tunnels and runner processes. ## 🏷️ Model and Skill Labels Labels let you control the workflow without editing YAML. ```text model/opencode/deepseek-v4.1-flash-free skill/load-sketchfab-threejs skill/gauntlet-loop ``` The workflow validates the selected labels, passes them into OpenCode, and records the resolved model and skills in the run logs. Shared skills are discovered from: ```text .agents/skills//SKILL.md ``` ## 🔄 OpenCode Workflow ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Trigger] --> B[Prepare project] B --> C[Run build.md] C --> D[Run verify.md] D --> E{Public app works?} E -- No --> F[Run public-app-fix.md] F --> E E -- Yes --> G[Run completion-report.md] G --> H{Screenshots exist?} H -- No --> I[Run screenshot-evidence.md] I --> H H -- Yes --> J[Commit and push] J --> K[Create immutable project link] K --> L[Publish report] L --> M[Complete] ``` ## 🏗️ Architecture ```text ┌──────────────┐ ┌─────────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ │ GitHub issue │ ──▶ │ GitHub Actions │ ──▶ │ OpenCode │ │ + issue text │ │ runner + labels │ │ + .agents │ └──────────────┘ └─────────────────┘ └──────┬───────┘ │ ┌─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ Build code Run tests Verify app │ │ │ └─────────────────────┼─────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌────────────────────────┐ │ Commit store + preview │ └────────────────────────┘ ``` ## 🔐 Security and Access - 🔑 You do not need to create or store a project-specific AI API key. - 🖥️ You do not need to operate a dedicated build server. - ☁️ Execution happens in GitHub Actions. - 🔒 Temporary SSH and preview access exists only for the workflow run. - 👀 Review the generated commit before integrating it. - 🛡️ Restrict who can apply the `OpenCode` label in repositories that accept public issues. > “No servers needed” means no servers for you to provision or maintain. The workflow still uses GitHub-hosted Actions infrastructure and temporary workflow services. ## 📁 Project Structure ```text 📦 OMG ├─ .github/workflows/opencode.yml # 🤖 Main issue-to-project workflow ├─ wiki/opencode.md # 📖 Workflow and session notes ├─ wiki/testing.md # 🧪 Verification guidance └─ AGENTS.md # 🧭 Repository instructions ``` ## 🧪 Local Validation Validate the workflow definition before pushing changes: ```sh actionlint .github/workflows/opencode.yml git diff --check ``` ## 🐛 Troubleshooting | Problem | What to check | |---|---| | The workflow did not start | Confirm the `OpenCode` label is applied to the issue. | | A skill was not selected | Add a matching `skill/` label. | | The app URL is missing | Check the local app verification step and runner log. | | The PR was not created | Confirm OpenCode produced a diff and the workflow reached the PR step. | | The workflow ran unexpectedly | Tighten the trigger condition and trusted-user policy. | ## 🤝 Contributing Ideas, skills, game templates, verification improvements, and workflow fixes are welcome. 1. Open an issue describing the improvement. 2. Add the `OpenCode` label when you want the workflow to prototype it. 3. Review the generated commit and Open Project page carefully. 4. Add tests and runtime proof for workflow changes. ## ⭐ The Pitch The old workflow was: idea → tickets → scaffolding → setup → implementation → debugging → deployment. The OMG workflow is: **idea → issue → playable project.** If you believe software should start with a sentence instead of a sprint plan, [⭐ star the repository](https://github.com/denaidark/OhMyGithub) and try it.

Usage: playwright-cli <command> [args] [options]

Core:
  open [url]                  open the browser
  attach [name]               attach to a running playwright browser
  close                       close the browser
  detach                      detach from an attached browser

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable 2D run-and-gun platformer where the player controls a badass American soldier, starts with a pistol, uses a dedicated knife key, unlocks better weapons across levels, and breaks barrels/crates for ammo and grenades.

## Requirements
- One-shot build request; do not ask clarifying questions.
- Reasonable assumptions should be made and briefly noted when finished.
- Game must be complete and playable now.
- Core requested mechanics: pistol start, dedicated knife key, weapon progression through levels, destructible barrels/crates dropping ammunition/grenades.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a dependency-free static Canvas 2D game served from `index.html`.
- Five hand-authored missions with escalating weapons: M1911 → MP5 → M870 → M4A1 → RPG-7.
- Added mouse aiming/click firing, `F`/`V` knife, `G` grenades, `R` reload, `Shift` combat roll, checkpoints, loot, drone/turret/heavy enemies, and a final Colonel Volkov boss.
- All visual art and audio are procedural; no external assets or fonts.
- Added full title screen, HUD, pause/death/level-clear/victory overlays, mobile touch controls, and localized procedural weather/themes.
- `playBtn` has `aria-label="Play"` so the screenshot runtime auto-start selector can find it.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created `index.html` with menu, HUD, overlays, boss bar, touch controls, and game canvas.
- Created `css/style.css` with full responsive tactical UI styling.
- Created `js/utils.js` with math/collision/time helpers.
- Created `js/audio.js` with synthesized weapons, explosions, pickups, ambience, and dynamic music.
- Created `js/levels.js` with weapon definitions and five full campaign levels.
- Created `js/renderer.js` with procedural skyline, parallax, weather, platforms, player/enemy/boss art, projectiles, explosions, particles, crosshair, and post FX.
- Created `js/game.js` with campaign flow, player physics, shooting/reload/knife/grenade/roll, enemy AI, boss logic, loot/checkpoints/hazards, HUD, and notifications.
- `node --check js/game.js` passes.

### Active
- Integration testing/debugging has not yet started.
- Need to patch known issues before browser verification:
  - Simplify redundant enemy firing condition around `js/game.js:1353`.
  - Remove `!this.touch.fire` from jump-cut check around `js/game.js:793`; jump cut should depend only on jump hold.
  - Reset `this.lastKillTime = -99` in `loadLevel`.
  - Clear `killFeed`, combo badge, and boss bar on level load.
  - Add checkpoint rendering; renderer currently has no `drawCheckpoint` call/function.
  - Hide crosshair on touch/mobile.
  - Review `drawBoss` phase/HP and gate transition behavior.
- Need to run locally and inspect desktop/mobile screenshots, then play-test interactions.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Apply the known code patches listed above.
2. Start the static server with `RUNTIME_DIR=/home/runner/work/_temp/omgithub-runtime PORT=3000 ./start.sh` in tmux.
3. Open with `playwright-cli`, click `PLAY`, and inspect screenshots at desktop and mobile sizes.
4. Test movement, firing, knife, grenades, reload, crate/barrel destruction, checkpoints, level completion, unlocks, death/retry, and final boss.
5. Fix runtime/console errors and visual defects from browser evidence.
6. Verify `git diff --check`, run a final screenshot pass, and briefly summarize assumptions/results in French.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: page structure, menu/HUD/overlays, `aria-label="Play"`.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/game.js`: main game loop, mechanics, AI, campaign flow, HUD.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/renderer.js`: all procedural Canvas rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/levels.js`: weapons, mission layouts, enemy/loot placement.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/audio.js`: synthesized audio engine.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/js/utils.js`: shared helper functions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/css/style.css`: complete responsive UI.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh`: project server entrypoint using `RUNTIME_DIR`.

## Important Context
- `js/game.js` exposes `window.__IRON_DAWN__ = this` for Playwright inspection/testing.
- Fixed timestep is `1/60`; renderer uses dynamic viewport with 720 world height.
- Auto-start detection matches a visible enabled button whose accessible label is exactly `Play`.
- The game must run through the runtime static server; `index.html` is project type `html`.
- Existing repo had only README/start scripts; all game files are currently uncommitted/untracked.
